Thanks for the report! This is an automated first-pass triage; a maintainer will make the final call.

**Reproduction:** not attempted: this is a style/feature request, and the issue gives no unexpected Black output to reproduce (the "current style" example is standard Black output).
**Assessment:** The behaviour described is deliberate. Black wraps lines uniformly and puts one element per line (with trailing commas) when a bracketed expression doesn't fit, which keeps diffs small. The style docs also say configuration options are deliberately limited and rarely added, so a new `no-short-lines` / `min-line-length` option runs against that design. See "How Black wraps lines" in the current style docs: (black.vercel.app/redacted) (docs at black.readthedocs.io, `the_black_code_style/current_style`).
**Next step:** Maintainers can weigh whether the proposal justifies a new option. Meanwhile, if you want to control the layout in specific places, removing the magic trailing comma lets Black collapse a collection that fits on one line.
